en.title: The URV and Brazil's Real Plan: Monetary Engineering, Inflation, Society and Power (1980–1999)
en.deck: How Brazil separated the unit of account from payments to dismantle inertial inflation—and why wage conversion, fiscal bargaining, banking, exchange rates and trust shaped the costs of stabilization.
keywords: Plano Real salary conversion four months
en.regime: An indexed high-inflation economy moves through a transitional unit of account to price stability under an initially exchange-supported real and, after 1999, inflation targeting.
en.key_risk: Confusing immediate disinflation with complete fiscal, banking and external sustainability, or treating nominal conversion as equal distributional benefit.

pt-BR.title: URV e Plano Real: a engenharia monetária que desarmou a inflação brasileira — e os custos de reconstruir uma moeda
pt-BR.deck: Da inflação inercial e da conversão de salários em URV à política fiscal, ao câmbio, aos bancos, às expectativas e à crise de 1999: como o Brasil recuperou uma unidade comum de valor.
pt-BR.regime: Economia com alta inflação indexada migra, por unidade de conta temporária, para estabilidade inicialmente apoiada por câmbio, e depois por metas de inflação.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir a queda imediata da inflação com sustentabilidade fiscal e externa completa ou concluir que uma simples divisão monetária determinou ganhos distributivos iguais.

contrary_evidence: 1992–1994 operational fiscal balances near zero according to Sachs/Zini weaken any simple claim that current deficit alone immediately sustained inflation.
High inflation reduced after July 1994 but monthly July IPCA 6.84% and 1995 IPCA 22.41% show no instantaneous zero inflation.
Initial price stability was accompanied by exchange appreciation, external deficit and high real interest rates; long-run sustainability required 1999 reforms.
Real incomes of low-income households improved in some 1995–1997 urban food-access studies but results diverged across regions, classes, job categories and after 1997.
URV was a legal unit of account, not a simultaneously circulating redeemable digital currency nor an irrevocable one-for-one US dollar currency-board commitment.
Former and later economic schools disagree about relative roles of fiscal restraint, inertia neutralization, trade competition and credibility; no identified causal shares are asserted.
limitations: Sources differ in definitions and periodization; annual 1994 inflation includes both currencies, and monthly versus 12-month inflation cannot be interchanged.
IPCA annual values use Ipeadata's series consistent with IBGE; rounding of 1994 can produce 916.43 vs 916.46 in different historical snapshots and vintages.
Fiscal and current-account period averages are historical measures under earlier accounting conventions and cannot be compared mechanically with later methods.
No econometric causal attribution of each URV, fiscal, exchange or interest channel; counterfactuals explicitly remain scenarios.
Claims of lower poverty and improved food affordability are limited by survey coverage and employment changes.
Historical interpretation uses secondary scholarship with contested readings; government explanations are treated as official policy rationale, not independent effect estimates.
Deployment of a public article requires independent SHA-bound QA approval, registration in editorial-system registry, seven-system reconciliation and successful CI plus live deployment.
